title: The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag show Wren their margins
summary: Samuel Wren comes to Cnoc bheag at the hawk-priests' asking and is shown their copy of his grammar, written in along every margin in the stag-letters. Beside his words keepers of the coal they have set the island's word three times, which means those who have the care of the vein. Wren copies all their notes by the priest's fire.

title: The custodian of Cnoc bheag answers Wren at the stakes
summary: At Carragh Cnoc bheag the custodian of the town tells Samuel Wren what her house has told every asker: the stone is older than the Dia-thìrich, the old schools' letters matched nothing on it, and the four words below were cut later by one who could read no more of it. Wren copies the line three times in the rain.

title: Wren blesses the striking-press at Ros dhomhain
summary: At Josiah Pell's asking Samuel Wren says a prayer over the new striking-press in its shed on the quay at Ros dhomhain, in the humans' tongue and then in Dia-thìris for the fishers watching at the door. The first mark is lifted from the die with tongs and dropped ringing in the tray.

title: Muireall's rubbing of the first mark sent to the loft
summary: Samuel Wren brings one of the first marks to Gormshuil nic Fhearchair in the long room of the council hall. Her niece Muireall takes a rubbing of both faces, writes beneath it that the island is on neither face, and the rubbing goes east that autumn with the season's copies to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol.

title: The market-clerk's sentence in both books
summary: Tadhg, the custodians' market-clerk at Cathair dhearg, keeps the dues of barter in one book and the dues in marks in another, and can make no single figure of them for the council. At the foot of each he writes that the one book cannot be added to the other, in the stag-letters and again in the humans' tongue.

title: The masters of Dùn thais invite Wren
summary: The masters of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh at Dùn thais write to Samuel Wren at Ros dhomhain, in the stag-letters, asking him to come for the dark of the year and dispute with them. He goes east with the carriers at the end of an t-Samhain, five days on the road through Cathair mhòr and the hills.

title: Wren's letter home on the druids
summary: From Dùn thais, in the last days of the year, Samuel Wren writes to the house of his order over the sea by the packet of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir. He sets down a tale the eldest master told at the hearth of a holy man's voyage west in a boat of hides, very like the voyage of Naomh Breandan as an Eaglais tells it, told from the other shore.

title: Queen Sìleas's stone set back in the bridge
summary: When the masons of A' Chompanaidh take down the parapets of Drochaid Cathair dhearg, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair asks the master mason to keep the block cut with Queen Sìleas's name. He has it dressed on its back and sides, its face left as it was, and sets it again in the new downstream parapet near the middle of the bridge.

title: Tormod mac Ailein walks behind the carriage
summary: Josiah Pell's carriage stops beside Tormod mac Ailein and Gormshuil nic Fhearchair on the new bridge, and Pell offers Ceann a' Chùraim a seat as far as the council hall. Tormod thanks him and answers aloud that they will walk, and the two custodians come up the hill on foot long after the carriage.

title: Gormshuil reads the harbour articles to the council
summary: Before the signing of Puingean a' Chalaidh, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads the eight sheets aloud to the council at Cathair dhearg, each clause first in the humans' tongue and then in Dia-thìris. Ailean Ruadh of Baile ghlas asks to hear the clause on the anchorages twice.

title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair refuses Puingean a' Chalaidh
summary: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair passes the sheet of Puingean a' Chalaidh on unsigned, and tells Josiah Pell in his own tongue that she will not put her name under what she has read. Ailean Ruadh of Baile ghlas refuses with her. The council's roll names the two, the first custodians to refuse a writing of the strangers.

title: The herring sold off the boats at Baile ghlas
summary: Having paid anchorage once, the fishermen of Baile ghlas sell their catch off the boats at their own jetty, to the fish-wives who walk out from the capital and to anyone but A' Chompanaidh, whose salting-house at Ros dhomhain has herring that season only from its own boats.

title: The first stone houses on the concession
summary: The human families granted summer grazing about Muileann àrsaidh build their houses of squared stone, with chimneys and slate. The custodian of Muileann àrsaidh writes to the council that the island's shielings are of turf and wattle for a summer, and asks whether the council meant the grant so.

title: The council's letter on the grazing
summary: At Tormod mac Ailein's sickbed Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads him the letter from Muileann àrsaidh. At his word she writes to the families on the grazing, in both tongues, that the council granted summer grazing and shielings, and sends it north the next morning.

title: Tormod mac Ailein waked three nights
summary: Tormod mac Ailein is waked three nights in his house below the temple at Cathair dhearg, by the old custom. On the second night the council, meeting below, chooses Coinneach Glas of Ceann àrsaidh in a single evening, and the roll enters the choice as unanimous.

title: Tormod mac Ailein buried at Cathair dhearg
summary: Six custodians carry Tormod mac Ailein to the ground behind the council hall, with the bells of the capital ringing, and the mourners lay their stones on the grave going round sunwise. Josiah Pell walks up from the bridge-foot bareheaded to stand at the edge of the ground. Samuel Wren stands at the gate.
